record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Which additional graph families G have the property that every completely positive realization A of G satisfies the Drew-Johnson-Loewy cp-rank bound cpr(A) <= floor(n^2/4), where n is the number of vertices of G and cpr(A) is the minimum number of columns in an entrywise nonnegative B with A = B B^T?

evidence.quote: Are there other graph families for which the DJL bound holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An n×n real symmetric matrix A is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative (not necessarily square) matrix B such that A = B B^T. The cp-rank of A, denoted cpr(A), is the smallest number of columns of such a matrix B. To a completely positive matrix A one associates its graph G(A) on vertex set {1,…,n}, in which {i,j} is an edge if and only if i ≠ j and A_{ij} > 0. For a graph G on n vertices, one says that G satisfies the Drew–Johnson–Loewy (DJL) bound if every n×n completely positive matrix A with G(A) = G satisfies cpr(A) ≤ ⌊n^2/4⌋.

It is known that several classes of graphs satisfy the DJL bound (for example, triangle-free graphs, graphs containing no odd cycle of length ≥ 5, and all non-complete graphs on 5 vertices), while the bound fails for general graphs in every dimension n ≥ 7.

Problem: Identify additional families of graphs G (beyond those already known) such that every completely positive matrix A whose graph equals G satisfies cpr(A) ≤ ⌊n^2/4⌋, where n is the number of vertices of G.
artifact.status_search_result: The DJL bound ⌊n^2/4⌋ is known to hold for triangle-free graphs, graphs with no odd cycle of length ≥ 5, and small cases (n ≤ 5), while Bomze–Schachinger–Ullrich disproved the general conjecture for n ≥ 7. The question of identifying further graph families satisfying the DJL bound remains an open program in the literature on completely positive matrices.

status_evidence.title: From seven to eleven: completely positive matrices with high cp-rank
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to the DJL conjecture in every dimension n ≥ 7, with maximal cp-rank of order n^2/2.
status_evidence.claim: DJL bound fails in general for n ≥ 7, motivating the search for graph families where it still holds.

status_evidence.title: On the cp-rank and minimal cp factorizations of a completely positive matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses cp-rank bounds and the DJL conjecture for various subclasses of completely positive matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Identifying graph families satisfying the DJL bound is an active research direction.
